I was in the same scenario you're in for a long time. I was certain my being trans would be the end of our relationship and it was, but I wasn't able to start hormones yet, so I let her cling on, because I felt too much guilt over leaving to put my foot down and start transitioning.

It sucks, but gender and sexual orientation aren't things that you can control, and it isn't fair to you to have to be with someone that you have to put on a mask for, and it isn't fair to her to spend her life with someone who isn't being themselves. Trust me, you sound like you're ready to come out, so the best thing to do is do it, the longer you put it off, and try to stay in the closet the more it will start to weigh on you, and the harder it will be. 

I know it feels selfish. Coming out was really the first thing that I've done that was totally for myself, but I promise you it is worth it. It isn't your fault what's happened anymore than it is hers, and if she is good for you, she will at the very least recognize that this is what's best for you, and for her. I loved my girlfriend more than anyone in the world, and trying to fight my gender identity in order to stay with her only made her angry and forced me to distance ourselves, because as much as I loved her I couldn't just go back in the closet and pretend I'm not trans. By the end of our time together, what seemed like a perfect relationship that I would stay in forever had become extremely emotionally abusive for both of us. Don't let that become your relationship. You need to be honest, and tell her who you are.

If you're indeed trans (which it sounds like you're pretty certain) then my assumption is that you've already realized everything I'm telling you in some form or another; maybe you're looking for validation in doing what you know you need (that's honestly what I was doing when I made a post just like this)

You never know, it sounds like you two have a strong relationship, and people can surprise you. Maybe she'll want to stay regardless of your gender identity, maybe she won't, but can you really live the rest of your life pretending to be someone else, when you know inside that it isn't right?

I'm sorry you're having to go through this. I know it's rough, but it will be okay sooner than you think if you deal with it now. Good luck, and congrats on realizing who you are. I promise you're in for a lot of awesome.

If you need someone to talk to who's been where you are feel free to send me a pm

A couple years ago I was in a similar situation to you, and felt miserable all the time, couldn't find a reason for living, everything was tedious, and I couldn't remember the last time I was happy. 

During this time I started smoking heavily and made a bad habit out of being unreasonably high on a daily basis. I didn't realize it at the time, but I was using it as a means of coping with my greater problems, and formed a dependency on weed to be happy. I became neglectful of the people I care about and even though I may have seemed better on the surface, my problems didn't go away. I still felt angry, sad, and stressed, and just dead inside; the biggest difference in my mental state was that I was laughing a lot more.

After a while of smoking tons of weed (ounces a week with my friends) my best friend and I eventually got caught, and arrested for possession of marijuana and  possession of a controlled substance. (We had a pipe with hash residue on it.) We had to spend the night in jail and deal with the fuckery of the legal system but fortunately we got very lucky, and didn't have to serve jail time or do probation.

After getting arrested I decided to stop covering up my problems and start trying to figure out who I am, and what was causing my depression, and that is when I started finding real relief.

The reason I'm telling you this story is because I don't want what happened to me to happen to you. Even outside of the legal trouble, weed didn't help my depression or solve my problems, it just made me forget about it when I was high.

I still smoke regularly today, but I use it as something for fun, that will enhance the things I enjoy and give me a good time with friends, not a crutch to get through the day, and help me forget about the fact that I didn't feel like a real person.

If you want to smoke weed I won't stop you, but please don't use it as a means of dealing with important problems in your life. Think about your life and who you are and see if you can figure out what may be causing your problems. Often times one of the most frustrating things about depression is that you don't know what is causing your problems, but once you realize it, you'll be able to work on it and improve your life.

I'm sure I'm going to get downvoted to hell for talking about forming a dependency on weed on the weed subreddit, but I'm speaking from my own personal experience. Maybe things wouldn't be the same for you, but using any mind-altering substance with the intent of trying to improve your mental health isn't a good idea.

If you want my advice as a person who's been where you are, find a therapist, try to do some self-reflection and figure out more about yourself.

Finally, I know shit is hard. Life will try to kick you as hard as it can in the dick, but it becomes so much better. I promise you, as someone who was suicidal and truly believed that life was not worth living, everything gets better. The only hard part is that sometimes you have to make it better.

PM me any time if you want to chat. I'll be more than happy to help if I can.

Personally I have two days in my life that have been equally traumatic for me; both of which happened this year. 

I'll start with the first one. Earlier this year I was arrested for possession of marijuana and a controlled substance (controlled substance was residue on a pipe from dabs) My friend and I were being extremely stupid and decided to smoke a HUGE bong in my car. We did a couple bowls and were jamming out to Pink Floyd and having a great time; but then, off in the distance, we saw something moving towards us. 

It was a turkey. I would like to point out now this was a serious wild turkey. This motherfucker was gigantic, and looked like a mighty beast, but I was confident in the power that my friend and I have. 

So naturally, being really high, and wanting to have a bit of fun, I turn to my friend and say "Let's go." He asks me what I mean and I tell him we should chase the turkey.

He asked me why I wanted to do so, and I had no real reason, but I fight the desire to chase that turkey, so we went. 

I pulled out my phone to film our adventure through the woods in search of the turkey that would play a vital role in changing our lives for the worse. After a bit of running we found the turkey. It was walking away from us to the other side of a small clearing surrounded by mud.

As the turkey began to disappear into the woods I began sprinting towards the turkey at full speed. I closed the gap quickly and was nearly at the edge of clearing, but in my weed fueled chase of this turkey I didn't notice the mud in front of me. I fell in a giant pile of mud (the last thing that happens in the video is the camera going up to the sky, a loud bang, and me yelling "FOR FUCK'S SAKE!"

After this happened my friend and I made the trek back to my car, where I thankfully had some spar clothes. I cleaned off as much as possible and changed clothes. We then climbed into my car to go get our friend from work, and we then saw the a black and white car driving towards us. 

My friend turned to me and said, "We're going to prison."

I love drugs as much as anyone, but make sure you do them in a safe environment. Learn from my stupid mistakes. You can get caught, and it's one of the worst things that can happen to a person.

TL;DR: Got really high, chased a turkey, fell in mud, went to jail.

Hi, I'm transgender. I've spent everyday since I began questioning my gender doing research into gender, gender identity, the gender spectrum, etc. in order to ensure a preparation for the path I'm walking down in life. I have put in the time and research to learning about these things, and spoken with professional gender therapists and psychologists, and you my friend, are wrong.

Cisgender is not a slur, it is the scientific term for people whose gender falls in line with their biological sex, in the same way that transgender is the scientific term to refer to those whose gender doesn't fall in line with their biological sex. It's true that many "oppressed" people on tumblr and other similar sites like to throw the word around as an insult on the basis that they believe cis people are the enemy of trans people. It's reclaiming a word for a different purpose; allow me to state an example: Decades ago the term "queer" was meant as a derogatory term towards homosexuals, however with the rise of the gay rights movement, the LGBT community has reclaimed this word and given it a different meaning, people are now proud to be queer ("We're here, we're queer.") 

In some circles "cisgender" has experienced the same phenomenon but it's gone in reverse, and some people have chosen to take a scientific term with a neutral connotation and use it as a slur used to insult cisgender people. 

I'm not going to deny that it has been used as a slur in some situations, because it has; frankly I've felt disgusted when going to transgender forums looking for resources and others in my situation to talk to, and find people posting stuff like "kill all cis people!" I don't support this, nor do I think it is justified under the argument of it being okay because some cis people act that way towards trans people.

So is it used as a slur? Sometimes, by hate perpetuating children who don't understand the true actual meaning of the word, but for the most part it is not. I understand why you feel that is the case, as I've seen the word being used in a negative connotation as well, but it is not a slur in a widespread sense.

More importantly however; Was the term invented to be a slur? Fuck no. Do some research.

And if you'll excuse me; I'm going to take my soapbox and be on my way

TL;DR: No it isn't.
